summary:
### TL;DR
- **Security risk assessments now run automatically for organizations on GitHub Team.** They are free and surface exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-18-security-risk-assessments-run-automatically-on-github-team))
- **Dependabot alert dismissal requests now expire after 1 year** under delegated dismissal. Older versions keep a 1-week expiry. Expired requests must be resubmitted. ([docs commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/53d128354cf59e192712dc42a4416cddedc08eaf))
- **Governance note:** Gemini 4 Neon is now GA in Copilot, including the Copilot coding agent and CLI. It is **automatically enabled** unless an admin has turned off the global default or disabled this model in the Copilot model policy. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-18-gemini-4-neon-in-github-copilot))

### Action required
Nothing this time.

### Security improvements
- **Automatic security risk assessments on GitHub Team:** Organization admins and security managers can review the findings to:
  - identify exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities,
  - understand the organization's current risk,
  - prioritize next steps.

  These cover both code security and secret risk assessments. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-18-security-risk-assessments-run-automatically-on-github-team); see also [Viewing your security risk assessment reports](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/configure-specific-tools/viewing-your-security-risk-assessment-reports))
- **Copilot model governance:** Copilot Business and Enterprise admins can manage access to Gemini 4 Neon through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default enablement, new models become available to users automatically. Teams with model allow-list requirements should check their policy settings. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-18-gemini-4-neon-in-github-copilot))

### Docs changes worth reading
- **[Enable delegated alert dismissal (Dependabot)](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/manage-security-alerts/manage-dependabot-alerts/enable-delegated-alert-dismissal):** The page now documents when dismissal requests expire:
  - **1 year** where the expiry feature is available,
  - **1 week** on versions without it.

  After expiry, a request must be resubmitted. Reviewers working through a backlog of dismissal requests should account for this. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/53d128354cf59e192712dc42a4416cddedc08eaf))
- The large commit "[Onboard five initiative journeys to docsTeamMetrics enforcement](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/8279f1d7f407f0015ece2b10ec217cdd8dfdc74d)" only adds internal `docsTeamMetrics` metadata tags to code quality and secret protection pages. There is no change in substance.

changelog.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
changelog.text: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work. According to Google, Gemini 4 Neon delivers quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task. Google also reports that, compared with Gemini 4 Carbon, it starts responding faster and makes fewer unrequested changes on coding tasks. It is also less likely to make unsupported claims about code, tool, or test results. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Neon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Neon through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team
changelog.text: GitHub security risk assessments now run automatically for organizations on GitHub Team. Organization admins and security managers can review findings from the free assessments to identify exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities, understand their organization’s current risk, and prioritize next steps. Read more about code security risk assessments and secret risk assessments . The post Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
